name: fig-03
title: fig-03: The cellular interface
confidence_basis: Calibrated off Provisional (workbench 0.4.1). BASELINE (fig03-runnable): each typed interface port responds to its own driver — but the review correctly notes the ports are INDEPENDENT (each a separate function of its driver), so this is typed-interface correctness, not coherent physiology, and is held at Medium. MECHANISTIC VARIANT (fig03-mechanistic, scientific-review revision) adds genuine multi-process coupling through a shared ATP pool + temperature-set enzyme activity: a single perturbation (heat shock or starvation) propagates to every downstream port (enzyme→uptake→ATP→growth→viability), the cross-port response matrix is dense, and a metabolically-disabled matched-null control breaks the propagation. The study stays Provisional because the coupling is demonstrated with didactic/toy-real rate laws (one lumped ATP pool, a Gaussian enzyme window, a basal maintenance drain) — not fitted to a measured respiration, maintenance coefficient, or growth-rate curve.
question: The paper's §Cellular interface (Fig cell_interface) defines a cell as an organization that senses and acts on its environment through typed PORTS -- "each port is a typed connection from the cell to a single variable in the shared state, with a type that fixes the units of what crosses it." Fig cell_interface a. shows interaction modalities as ports (nutrient exchange, motile force, growth, electrical signaling); Fig cell_interface b. shows a minimal interface combining physical exchange ports with higher-level cellular variables (growth, shape, objectives, viability bounds). Is that interface EXECUTABLE rather than merely drawn -- i.e. does a runnable process-bigraph composite exercise those typed ports so that each port's value RESPONDS to its driving environmental input, demonstrating the typed cell -> shared-variable connection the caption asserts?
biological_summary:
This study makes Fig cell_interface runnable. The `fig03-runnable` composite (`meta_modelers_guide.composites.fig03-runnable`) wires ONE bounded cell (`CellularInterfaceHandler`, a conforming process-bigraph Process) to an environment that supplies four typed drivers -- a chemical concentration, a mechanical force, an electrical voltage, and a thermal temperature -- and reads back the cell's typed interface ports: the physical exchange ports (chemical flux, mechanical force, electrical current, thermal heat flux) plus the higher-level cellular variables the caption names -- growth_rate, shape (volume), signaling, objective, and viability.
Each port is a typed connection from the cell to a single shared variable (paper: W(cell,q)=p with type Sigma(p)), and the demonstration is that the ports RESPOND: a higher chemical supply drives a proportionally larger uptake flux and (via Monod) a larger growth rate; the mechanical, electrical, and thermal exchange ports each track their own driver through a plausible linear response law (elastic force, Ohmic current, Fourier heat flux) and stay put when their driver is off; the cell accretes shape (volume) as it grows; and viability -- the higher-level variable that says whether the cellular description still holds -- declines by first-order Arrhenius thermal death when the environment is held ABOVE the cell's 37 C optimum. The runnable composite seeds the thermal driver at 45 C (above optimum) so viability visibly falls over the run, the cell taking up chemical and growing while its viability bound is being pushed toward collapse. This is Fig cell_interface b. in action: the environment's drivers drive the cell's typed interface ports, over time, through the process-bigraph engine.
The interface here is DIDACTIC / toy-real: the response laws (uptake_rate, Monod km, elasticity, membrane conductance, thermal conductance) and the Arrhenius thermal-death constants are plausible, hand-chosen magnitudes -- pinned so the D-value is ~1 min at the 55 C E. coli thermal-death reference and negligible near 37 C -- chosen to make each port's response legible in a short run, not calibrated to a named cell type or a literature dataset. The rigorous, mechanism-independent treatment of this same interface -- specifying the cell as nothing but typed unit-bearing ports, compiling a conforming handler into the draft, and MEASURING that two different internal mechanisms realize the same interface relation to within tolerance -- is its cousin `cellular-interface` in the `draft-to-living-cell` investigation; this study's job is only to show the caption's ports RESPOND, runnably.
claim: Fig cell_interface is executable: composing one bounded cell (`CellularInterfaceHandler`) with a four-driver environment through the `fig03-runnable` composite exercises the caption's typed interface ports so that each port's value responds to its driving input, demonstrating the typed cell -> shared-variable connection the paper asserts. Deterministically: a 5x higher chemical supply (0.2 -> 1.0) produces exactly a 5x larger uptake flux (-0.16 -> -0.80) and a strictly larger Monod growth rate (0.171 -> 0.400); the mechanical, electrical, and thermal exchange ports each respond linearly to their own driver and read zero when it is off; the cell accretes shape (volume 1.0 -> 10.6) as it grows over the 24-step run; and with the thermal driver held at 45 C (above the 37 C optimum) viability falls strictly monotonically from 1.0 to 0.175 by Arrhenius thermal death, whereas at the 37 C optimum it barely moves (1.0 -> 0.911, a decline < 0.1) -- isolating temperature as the cause. Every number is a deterministic function of the handler's response laws and reproduces exactly run to run.

variants.name: fig03-mechanistic
variants.rationale: Real-mechanism upgrade (scientific-review revision, Oct 2026). The baseline fig03-runnable realizes each interface port as an INDEPENDENT function of its own driver (uptake ∝ nutrient, growth = Monod(nutrient), viability = Arrhenius(T)); the ports never interact, so "the interface responds" says nothing about coherent physiology — the review's objection. This variant (MetabolicCell + EnvironmentStep, handlers_fig03_mech.py) COUPLES the ports through TWO shared internal state variables — an ATP pool and a temperature-set enzyme activity: nutrient → (enzyme-limited saturating) uptake → ATP production; ATP → growth (anabolism) AND a basal maintenance drain; temperature → enzyme activity → uptake AND growth; an ATP deficit (production < maintenance) OR heat → viability decline; viability gates growth. A single perturbation (a 37→48 °C heat shock, or a nutrient step-down) therefore PROPAGATES to every downstream port, and a metabolically-disabled cell (catalytic_capacity = ε) breaks the propagation (the matched-null control). The baseline is kept intact as the didactic smoke test.

key_assumptions: The `fig03-runnable` composite is DIDACTIC / toy-real: it is built to look like Fig cell_interface and play forward, NOT calibrated to a named cell type or literature dataset. The response-law constants (uptake_rate 0.8, growth_max 0.6, Monod km 0.5, elasticity 0.1, membrane_conductance 0.05, thermal_conductance 0.02, signaling_gain 0.4) are plausible, hand-chosen magnitudes selected to make each port's response legible in a 24-step run.

The Arrhenius thermal-death law (k(T)=A*exp(-Ea/RT), dV/dt=-k(T)*V, Ea~=300 kJ/mol) is a genuine functional form, but its constants are pinned to a reference target, not fitted to data: A is set so the D-value (time for a 1-log kill) is ~1 min at the 55 C E. coli thermal-death reference, which makes death negligible near 37 C (D ~ 10 h) and severe above it. The 45 C driver in the runnable composite is chosen so viability visibly falls within the run.

Every port in this study is a single lumped cell's response law -- there is no space, no membrane geometry, and no molecular detail. The interface is exactly the paper's coarse-grained representation: internal processes are not resolved, only their effects on the shared typed variables (metabolism as exchange flux, motility as force, growth as an accreting volume).

The instantaneous ports (chemical, mechanical, electrical, thermal, growth_rate, signaling) are written with "set" semantics over process-bigraph's accumulate-by-default stores; only shape and objective are genuine accumulating pools. The emitter's first row (tick 0) therefore reads 0 for the set-semantics ports before the first update, which is a recording artifact of the initial state, not a dynamical fact.

This study demonstrates only that the caption's ports RESPOND, runnably. It does NOT claim mechanism-independence, unit-correctness of a real cell, or calibration. The rigorous spatial/compositional cousin that specifies the interface as typed unit-bearing ports and MEASURES that two different internal mechanisms realize the same interface relation is `cellular-interface` in the `draft-to-living-cell` investigation.
acceptance_criteria: A higher chemical supply drives a proportionally larger uptake flux AND a strictly larger Monod growth rate -- the chemical exchange port and the growth port respond to their driver.

Each physical exchange port (mechanical force, electrical current, thermal heat flux) responds to its OWN driver linearly and in isolation, reading zero when that driver is off -- a typed connection from the cell to one shared variable.
The higher-level `shape` (volume) port accretes monotonically as the cell grows -- a higher-level cellular variable responding to sustained uptake.

With the thermal driver held ABOVE the cell''s optimum, the `viability` port falls strictly monotonically (Arrhenius thermal death), whereas at the optimum it barely changes -- the viability-bound variable responding to temperature, with temperature isolated as the cause.

units_and_time.time: 1 step = 1 minute of model time (the thermal-death constants are pinned in minutes); the runnable composite runs 24 such steps.
units_and_time.quantities: chemical_ext is a concentration and chemical flux is its negated uptake; mechanical is force, electrical is current, thermal is a heat flux, temperature is in C (converted to K internally for Arrhenius); growth_rate is a specific rate, shape a volume, objective a biomass proxy, viability a dimensionless [0,1] fraction. The magnitudes are toy-real model units, not calibrated to a physical cell.
units_and_time.note: No quantity here is calibrated to a named cell type, material, or literature target; the thermal-death form is pinned to an E. coli reference D-value, not fitted.

findings.statement: Fig cell_interface is executable, not merely drawn: composing one bounded cell (`CellularInterfaceHandler`) with a four-driver environment through the `fig03-runnable` composite exercises the caption's typed interface ports so each responds to its driving input. The chemical exchange port and the growth port respond to chemical supply (a 5x supply gives exactly 5x uptake flux and a strictly larger Monod growth rate); the mechanical, electrical, and thermal exchange ports each respond linearly to their own driver and read zero when it is off; and the higher-level shape (volume) port accretes strictly (1.0 -> 10.6) as the cell grows. Each is a deterministic typed cell -> shared-variable connection.

evidence.observed: flux ratio 5.0; force 0.2 / current 0.15 / heat flux 0.2 under their drivers, 0 at rest; shape 1.0 -> 10.6

findings.statement: The higher-level viability-bound variable of Fig cell_interface b. responds to its thermal driver: with the temperature held above the 37 C optimum (45 C) viability falls strictly monotonically by first-order Arrhenius thermal death from 1.0 to 0.175, whereas at the 37 C optimum it barely moves (ends 0.911, decline < 0.1). The paired runs isolate temperature as the cause -- final viability differs by 0.736 between the two -- demonstrating the interface's viability bound as a runnable, driver-responsive port rather than a drawn label. Toy-real: the death constants are pinned to an E. coli reference D-value, not fitted.

evidence.observed: viability 1.0 -> 0.175 at 45 C; 1.0 -> 0.911 at 37 C; final gap 0.736

findings.statement: The two measured growth-rate points jointly recover the handler's Monod constants exactly, so the growth port is a genuine saturating response, not a linear proxy. Growth at chemical supply 0.2 is 0.17143 and at supply 1.0 is 0.40000; both satisfy mu = growth_max * S / (S + km) with growth_max = 0.6 and km = 0.5 to 1e-5 (0.6*0.2/0.7 = 0.17143; 0.6*1.0/1.5 = 0.40000). Because growth saturates while uptake flux stays strictly linear in supply (ratio exactly 5.0 across the same 0.2->1.0 change), the growth and uptake ports are measurably different functional forms driven by the one chemical input -- the interface exposes two distinct, recoverable response laws, confirmed in-memory on a fresh CellularInterfaceHandler.

evidence.observed: growth 0.17143 (S=0.2) and 0.40000 (S=1.0) both == 0.6*S/(S+0.5); uptake-flux ratio exactly 5.0 (linear) over the same change

provenance.analysis_script: in-memory CellularInterfaceHandler driven at paired supplies 0.2 vs 1.0 (workbench 0.4.1)

findings.statement: The interface ports are genuinely COUPLED through shared internal state, fixing the review's objection that the baseline's ports each respond only to their own driver. In the mechanistic variant a single perturbation propagates: a 37→48 °C heat shock drops enzyme activity 1.00→0.22, which cascades through uptake and ATP to collapse growth 0.43→0.07 AND erode viability 1.00→0.43 — one input moving every downstream port. A nutrient step-down propagates the same way (growth→0.07, ATP→0, viability→0.24). The cross-port response matrix is dense (a temperature perturbation moves all four measured outputs), not diagonal. This is physiological coupling, not nine independent driver responses.

evidence.observed: heat shock → enzyme 1.00→0.22, growth 0.43→0.07, viability 1.00→0.43; starvation → growth→0.07, ATP→0, viability→0.24

findings.statement: The coupling is demonstrably THROUGH the shared ATP node, not direct wiring — shown by a matched-null ablation. With metabolism disabled (catalytic_capacity = ε, not 0.0), the cell cannot turn nutrient into ATP, so growth stays ~0 and biomass stays flat regardless of nutrient supply: the propagation breaks exactly where the shared energy currency is removed. Growth is paid out of ATP (it collapses when the ATP pool is depleted), and the shared state stays well-posed (ATP ≥ 0, viability ∈ [0,1], biomass monotone). Honest scope: typed-interface CORRECTNESS (each port responds) was already shown by the baseline; what the variant adds is genuine multi-process physiological COUPLING — but the rate laws and constants remain didactic/toy-real (one lumped ATP pool, a Gaussian enzyme window, a basal maintenance drain), not fitted to a measured respiration or growth-rate curve.

evidence.observed: disabled cell growth ≈ 0, biomass flat 1.0, nutrient change moves biomass <1e-3; growth→0 at ATP minimum

biological_validation.basis: Reported in two layers, per the review. BEHAVIORAL (baseline fig03-runnable): all six primary behavior tests pass — each typed port responds to its own driver, with paired optimum/above-optimum runs isolating temperature for the viability decline. This establishes typed-interface CORRECTNESS, but the ports are independent, so it is NOT evidence of coherent physiology. MECHANISTIC (variant fig03-mechanistic): the ports are coupled through a shared ATP pool + enzyme activity, so a single perturbation propagates to every downstream port (mechanistic_ablation), the cross-port response matrix is dense, the state stays bounded and growth is paid out of ATP (invariant), and a metabolically-disabled matched-null control breaks the propagation. This is genuine multi-process physiological coupling. NOT yet empirical validation against a measured respiration/maintenance/growth curve — that is the stated next step.

explanatory_gain.basis: Making Fig cell_interface runnable turns the caption's static ports into a demonstration that each typed port's value CHANGES in response to its driving variable -- the paper's "typed connection from the cell to a single variable in the shared state" shown playing forward through the engine, one lumped cell, drivers -> ports over time.

conclusion:
## Claims
- Fig cell_interface is executable: the `fig03-runnable` composite exercises the caption's typed interface ports so each responds to its driving input. A 5x chemical supply gives exactly 5x uptake flux (-0.16 -> -0.80) and a strictly larger Monod growth rate (0.171 -> 0.400); the mechanical, electrical, and thermal exchange ports respond linearly to their own driver (force 0.2, current 0.15, heat flux 0.2) and read zero when it is off; the higher-level shape (volume) port accretes strictly from 1.0 to 10.6 over the 24-step run.
- The viability-bound variable responds to temperature: held at 45 C (above the 37 C optimum) viability falls strictly monotonically from 1.0 to 0.175 by Arrhenius thermal death, while at the optimum it barely changes (ends 0.911, decline < 0.1). Paired runs isolate temperature as the cause -- a 0.736 gap in final viability.
- Every number is a deterministic function of the handler's response laws and reproduces exactly run to run.

## Evidence
- **HIGHER-CHEMICAL-DRIVES-UPTAKE-AND-GROWTH** -- flux ratio exactly 5.0; growth 0.171 -> 0.400
- **PHYSICAL-PORTS-RESPOND-TO-THEIR-DRIVERS** -- force 0.2, current 0.15, heat flux 0.2; all 0 at rest
- **SHAPE-ACCRETES-WITH-GROWTH** -- shape 1.0 -> 10.6, strictly increasing
- **ABOVE-OPTIMUM-DRIVES-VIABILITY-DOWN** -- viability 1.0 -> 0.175 (< 0.5), strictly decreasing
- **AT-OPTIMUM-VIABILITY-HOLDS** -- viability ends 0.911 (> 0.9), decline 0.089
- **HOTTER-KILLS-FASTER-THAN-OPTIMUM** -- final gap 0.736 (0.911 vs 0.175)

## Limitations
- The `fig03-runnable` composite is didactic / toy-real: the response-law constants and the Arrhenius thermal-death constants are plausible, hand-chosen magnitudes (the death form pinned to an E. coli reference D-value), not calibrated to a named cell type or literature dataset.
- It is one lumped cell with no space, membrane geometry, or molecular detail -- exactly the paper's coarse-grained interface, internal processes represented only through their effects on the shared typed variables.
- This study demonstrates only that the caption's ports RESPOND, runnably; it does not claim mechanism-independence or calibration. The rigorous cousin that specifies the interface as typed unit-bearing ports and measures that two different internal mechanisms realize the same interface relation is `cellular-interface` in the `draft-to-living-cell` investigation.

## Next steps
- Read this alongside the calibrated cousin `cellular-interface` to compare the same interface at didactic vs mechanism-independent rigor.
- Fan out to the next figure's runnable study in the `paper-figures` investigation.

diagnose: the chemical/growth ports do not scale with supply (the Monod or first-order uptake law is mis-wired, or the driver is not reaching the handler input)
a physical exchange port does not track its driver or leaks onto a non-driven port (the linear response law or the port wiring is broken)
shape fails to accrete (growth is not driving the accumulating volume pool)
viability does not fall at 45 C, or falls at 37 C too (the Arrhenius thermal-death law or its temperature reference is mis-pinned)
if_primary_tests_fail.block_downstream: any figure study reusing the CellularInterfaceHandler response laws or the drivers -> typed-ports demonstration pattern

limitations: The `fig03-runnable` composite is didactic / toy-real: the response-law constants (uptake_rate 0.8, growth_max 0.6, km 0.5, elasticity 0.1, membrane_conductance 0.05, thermal_conductance 0.02, signaling_gain 0.4) are plausible, hand-chosen magnitudes chosen to make each port's response legible in a 24-step run, not calibrated to a named cell type or literature dataset.

The Arrhenius thermal-death form is genuine but its constants are pinned to a reference, not fitted: A is set so the D-value is ~1 min at the 55 C E. coli thermal-death reference (negligible near 37 C, severe above it), and the 45 C driver is chosen so viability visibly falls within the run.

It is one lumped cell with no space, membrane geometry, or molecular detail -- the paper's coarse-grained interface, internal processes represented only through their effects on the shared typed variables.

The instantaneous ports use "set" semantics over accumulate-by-default stores, so the emitter's first row (tick 0) reads 0 for those ports before the first update -- a recording artifact of the initial state, not a dynamical fact.

This study demonstrates only that the caption's ports RESPOND, runnably. The rigorous cousin that specifies the interface as typed unit-bearing ports and MEASURES that two different internal mechanisms realize the same interface relation to within tolerance is `cellular-interface` in the `draft-to-living-cell` investigation; its numbers are not restated here as this study's own.

Mechanistic variant (fig03-mechanistic) — scope and honest limits: it adds genuine multi-process coupling (shared ATP pool + enzyme activity, propagation, matched-null control), fixing the baseline's independent-port limitation. But it is still ONE lumped cell with no space/membrane geometry/molecular detail; the ATP pool, the Gaussian enzyme-activity window, the basal maintenance drain, and the viability stress law are didactic/toy-real forms, NOT fitted to a measured respiration rate, maintenance coefficient (m_ATP), growth yield, or thermal-inactivation curve. The cross-port response matrix's nutrient row is an instantaneous one-step proxy (growth responds over ticks, not in one step), so it understates the nutrient→growth coupling that the time-series clearly shows. Empirical calibration remains the sibling investigation's job.
falsifiability: Overturned if a higher chemical supply fails to give a proportionally larger uptake flux or a larger growth rate, if any physical exchange port fails to respond to its own driver or responds to a driver that is off, if shape fails to accrete as the cell grows, if viability fails to fall strictly at 45 C, if viability falls substantially at the 37 C optimum, or if any of these readouts stops being deterministic across repeated runs of the same composite.

visualizations.name: Figure 3 · the paper's process-bigraph diagram (panel b)

config.caption: The paper's panel-b diagram for Fig 3 (the minimal cellular interface): a cell exposes physical exchange ports (chemical, mechanical, electrical, thermal) and higher-level cellular ports (growth rate, shape, signaling, objective, viability).

Baseline (didactic smoke test): the simpler pre-revision model — a bounded cell whose typed ports respond to environmental drivers INDEPENDENTLY. A chemical supply drives Monod uptake and growth, while a thermal driver held above the 37 °C optimum drives viability down by first-order thermal death. Kept as the executable baseline; the mechanistic figure below couples the ports through a shared ATP/enzyme state so a perturbation propagates. From scripts/build_fig03_dynamics.py.

Mechanistic (the decisive figure): the ports are now coupled through a shared ATP/enzyme state, so a perturbation propagates. What to look for: (A) a single 37→48 °C heat shock at t=12 cascades through the shared state to EVERY downstream port — enzyme activity, uptake, growth and viability all drop together; (B) a membrane cross-section with the simulated port flows before vs after the shock (uptake 0.80→0.18, growth 0.43→0.10, viability 1.00→0.93 and falling); (C) a nutrient step-down (2.0→0.03) drives the same cascade through ATP; (D) the cross-port response matrix — perturbing one input moves MULTIPLE outputs (a temperature step moves all four), the off-diagonal coupling IS the shared internal state, unlike the baseline's independent per-port responses; (E) disabling metabolism (catalytic_capacity = ε) breaks the propagation — biomass stays flat; (F) the ATP budget — growth is paid out of the shared ATP pool against a basal maintenance demand. From scripts/build_fig03_mechanistic.py.

experiment: Run the `fig03-runnable` composite (`CellularInterfaceHandler`, one bounded cell wired to a four-driver environment: chemical supply 1.0, thermal driver 45 C above the 37 C optimum) for 24 steps through the process-bigraph engine, and additionally drive a fresh handler at paired chemical supplies (0.2 vs 1.0) and paired temperatures (45 C vs 37 C), to measure whether each typed interface port's value responds to its driving environmental input as Fig cell_interface asserts.
result: Fig cell_interface is executable. A 5x chemical supply (0.2 -> 1.0) gives exactly a 5x uptake flux (-0.16 -> -0.80) and a strictly larger Monod growth rate (0.171 -> 0.400); the mechanical, electrical, and thermal exchange ports each respond linearly to their own driver (force 0.2, current 0.15, heat flux 0.2) and read zero when it is off; the higher-level shape (volume) port accretes strictly from 1.0 to 10.6 over the 24-step run; and with the thermal driver held at 45 C above the 37 C optimum, viability falls strictly monotonically from 1.0 to 0.175 by Arrhenius thermal death, whereas at the optimum it barely moves (ends 0.911, decline < 0.1) -- a 0.736 gap in final viability isolating temperature as the cause. Every number is a deterministic function of the handler's response laws and reproduces exactly run to run. The composite is didactic / toy-real (uncalibrated); the rigorous, mechanism-independent treatment of this same interface is the cousin `cellular-interface` in the `draft-to-living-cell` investigation.

biological_validation.basis: Reported in two layers, per the review. BEHAVIORAL (baseline fig03-runnable): all six primary behavior tests pass — each typed port responds to its own driver, with paired optimum/above-optimum runs isolating temperature for the viability decline. This establishes typed-interface CORRECTNESS, but the ports are independent, so it is NOT evidence of coherent physiology. MECHANISTIC (variant fig03-mechanistic): the ports are coupled through a shared ATP pool + enzyme activity, so a single perturbation propagates to every downstream port (mechanistic_ablation), the cross-port response matrix is dense, the state stays bounded and growth is paid out of ATP (invariant), and a metabolically-disabled matched-null control breaks the propagation. This is genuine multi-process physiological coupling. NOT yet empirical validation against a measured respiration/maintenance/growth curve — that is the stated next step.

regression_compatibility.basis: fig03-runnable.composite.json builds and runs 24 steps to completion through the process-bigraph engine, and the conforming `CellularInterfaceHandler` compiles against the cellular-interface signature (tests/test_fig03_interface_responds.py, and the companion conformance/spatial tests referenced in the handler module).

explanatory_gain.basis: Making Fig cell_interface runnable turns the caption's static ports into a demonstration that each typed port's value CHANGES in response to its driving variable -- the paper's "typed connection from the cell to a single variable in the shared state" shown playing forward through the engine, one lumped cell, drivers -> ports over time.

derived.insight: Fig cell_interface is executable, not merely drawn: composing one bounded cell (`CellularInterfaceHandler`) with a four-driver environment through the `fig03-runnable` composite exercises the caption's typed interface ports so each responds to its driving input. The chemical exchange port and the growth port respond to chemical supply (a 5x supply gives exactly 5x uptake flux and a strictly larger Monod growth rate); the mechanical, electrical, and thermal exchange ports each respond linearly to their own driver and read zero when it is off; and the higher-level shape (volume) port accretes strictly (1.0 -> 10.6) as the cell grows. Each is a deterministic typed cell -> shared-variable connection.
